correctness.rationale: For any fixed nondegenerate convex polygon, circumradius≤t forces pairwise distances≤2t. Compactness and absence of noncollinear same-edge triples localize sufficiently small triangles at one vertex on its two incident rays; finite positive threshold depends on the polygon. For two ordered ray coordinates a,b and one c the exact circumradius factor is sqrt(a²+c²−2ac cosθ)sqrt(b²+c²−2bc cosθ)/(2c sinθ); substituting a=cu,b=cv with Jacobian c² gives an integral of 8t³ sin³θ/3 times the square of an explicit 1D integral (1+cosθ)/sin²θ. Exactly six ordered assignments across two rays yield factor 16t³(1+cosθ)²/sinθ per vertex, including the collinear positive-mass atom at +∞ outside the event. Exterior turns δ_i sum to 2π and the angle score f(δ)=2tan³(δ/2)/(1+tan²(δ/2)) has f″=tan(δ/2)(1+tan²(δ/2))+2tan(δ/2)/(1+tan²(δ/2))>0. Exact symbolic differentiation independently checked this identity, proving Jensen and equality exactly at equiangular polygons. Regular m-gon formula agrees algebraically. Checker.py uses finite quadrature and MC only as diagnostics.
